body.target_estimand: \(\{P_x^D(Y=y):D\in\mathfrak D\}\), together with its equality quotient on \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\)
body.estimand_functional: For every returned class \(C\) with representative \(R_C\), \(P_x^D(Y=y)=T_{D,y}(p)=T_{R_C,y}(p)\) for every \(D\in C\) and \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) under a compatible Markovian SCM; when there is one class this is the common law \(P_x(Y=y)\).

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from one fixed strictly positive multinomial law \(P\) after a real-realizable exact oracle, its computed tied family, and one returned effect class have been fixed; a common-effect analysis uses the one-class case.
sampling_model.units: The observations \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) are independent draws in the finite cell space \(\Omega\).
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention \(do(X=x)\) is a causal query, not a randomized sampling arm.
sampling_model.overlap: Membership \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) gives positive cells and positive recorded marginal denominators at the fixed law.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no nonparametric nuisances; \(\widehat\tau_n=\tau(\widehat p_n)\) and \(\widehat V_n=J_{\tau}(\widehat p_n)\{\operatorname{diag}(\widehat p_n)-\widehat p_n\widehat p_n^{\mathsf T}\}J_{\tau}(\widehat p_n)^{\mathsf T}\) are computed from the fixed certified circuit.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.2 gives a sufficient graphical condition for simultaneous identification over a finite SA-MPDAG family.

Theorem 3.6 gives a necessary-and-sufficient criterion and generalized truncated factorization for one MPDAG; the present proof uses only the graph-specific functional substrate and makes no extensional-equivalence claim.
Theorem 8 identifies a DAG factorization component by saturation of local and global Markov ideals.

Theorem 3 minimally enumerates distinct intervention functionals represented by one MPDAG; any class it certifies as one graph-generic functional is contained in a SparseSIM-ID class when the exact-oracle model lies in that MPDAG Markov model, with no converse claimed.
IDP is sound and complete for causal-effect identification from one PAG.
A discrete causal query under one specified model compiles to a sharp polynomial program with anytime-valid outer bounds.
Resampling CI statistics and unioning graphwise intervals yields asymptotically correct coverage for a fixed effect after PC discovery.
SP consistently recovers the true MEC under the sparsest Markov representation condition; the present algorithm instead retains every minimum-edge I-map tie before quotienting by the causal query.

body.tldr: SparseSIM-ID no longer assumes a supplied positive rational realization or a supplied complete graph family. From a finite exact CI oracle and background orientations it first certifies oracle realizability, exhaustively constructs every minimum-edge DAG I-map unless a valid compressed certificate is supplied, and computes the unique coarsest quotient of the tied family whose classes share the same \(P_x(Y)\) functional on the strictly positive exact-oracle model. It returns one observable circuit per class, exact within-class equality certificates, and an exact real-algebraic positive ambiguity table for every class pair. Normalization reduces the full pairwise feasibility count to \(\binom{|\mathfrak D|}{2}(\prod_{v\in Y}|\Omega_v|-1)\); the one-reference common-effect test uses \((|\mathfrak D|-1)(\prod_{v\in Y}|\Omega_v|-1)\). The four-binary-variable rational witness and fixed-circuit plug-in inference are preserved.

project_justification.gap: Existing simultaneous-identification criteria are sufficient graphical tests and do not compute the maximal law-restricted effect quotient across all tied minimum-edge DAG I-maps. Saturated CI ideals also do not select strict positivity or the bit-zero exact-oracle chamber.
project_justification.niche: For finite observed variables, the exact oracle, all admissible DAGs, every graphwise truncated functional, and every positive-chamber equality test are finite and exact. This makes the tied-sparsest family itself computable and supports a graph-native maximal quotient rather than arbitrary selection of one tie.
project_justification.fill: The project gives a terminating realizability-first algorithm that enumerates all minimum-edge I-map ties, partitions them by universal equality of their causal distributions on the strictly positive exact-oracle model, and certifies every merge or separation. It exposes reduced reference and all-pairs decision counts, preserves real-radical zero tests only as an optional fast equality branch, and returns algebraic-number ambiguity witnesses whenever classes differ.

body.related_work: Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo (2025, Theorem 3.2 and Section 4.2) give the closest simultaneous-identification boundary: their SA-MPDAG condition is sufficient, whereas SparseSIM-ID decides and certifies the complete effect quotient of every finite tied minimum-edge I-map family. The preserved four-node rational example lies outside that graphical sufficient region and has two distinct causal values. Perkovic (2020, Theorem 3.6) supplies single-MPDAG identification structure, but no extensional equivalence with the present law-restricted cross-family quotient is claimed. Guo and Perkovic (2021, Theorem 3) minimally enumerate graph-generic effect functionals within one MPDAG; the proved relation is one-way: a class they certify as one functional is contained in a SparseSIM-ID class whenever the exact-oracle model is contained in that MPDAG's positive Markov model. Garcia, Stillman, and Sturmfels (2005) inform saturation, while Tarski's decision method and Stengle's Positivstellensatz provide supporting exact feasibility machinery rather than the causal novelty. Kahle, Rauh, and Sullivant (2017) explain why irrelevant CI components preclude reading positive exact-oracle separation from ideal nonmembership. Raskutti and Uhler (2018) motivate retention of all sparsest ties; the new output policy quotients those ties by the causal query. Jaber, Zhang, and Bareinboim (2019), Duarte et al. (2024), and Chang, Guo, and Malinsky (2024) remain adjacent completeness, optimization, and post-selection comparators rather than equivalent results.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Termination and the numbers of positive-chamber comparisons are explicit, but no favorable running-time, degree, certificate-length, or algebraic-height bound is claimed. The default DAG enumeration is finite and may be exponential or worse. Saturation by cells and denominators excludes components contained in their zero sets but imposes neither positivity nor bit-zero nonvanishing, so a nonzero normal form is only a feasibility trigger. General feasible separators are guaranteed to be exact real algebraic, not rational. The remaining rational-output question asks only whether an actually feasible set \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\{F_{D,D',y}\neq0\}\) always contains a bounded-height rational point; it is not needed for correctness or completeness of the decision theorem.
body.honest_scope: The required inputs are finite state spaces, a complete exact CI bit-vector, background orientations, and a query. A rational realization and a compressed SA-MPDAG or CPDAG family are optional checked accelerators, not assumptions. Unrealizable exact oracles and background systems admitting no I-map receive finite rejection certificates; every real-realizable oracle with at least one admissible DAG proceeds to the complete tied minimum-edge quotient. Separators are exact real algebraic unless an optional rational sample succeeds, and no polynomial-time or uniform height guarantee is made. The quotient is law-restricted and can be coarser than a graph-generic within-MPDAG enumeration; only the proved one-way Guo--Perkovic containment is claimed. The four-variable table remains an explicit rational cross-MEC separator with values \(13/20\) and \(1/2\). Plug-in inference is pointwise for a fixed returned circuit and is not selection-aware inference for an estimated oracle or tie family.
